prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Offshore wind farm O&M concept; scope: offshore assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel, external orgs, electrical up to Grid Interface Relay (gives normal-supply/protection status); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): executes authorized control, limits output, blocks protection-conflicting commands, reports state, enters safe mode when auxiliary services unavailable; produces Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (interlocks), Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur): blade imagery. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers (MV collection feeds auxiliary loads; essential/nonessential separated); Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-starts on auxiliary loss, transfers to emergency distribution bus only when voltage/frequency within limits, no paralleling without approved synchronizing, no export support; prioritized loads; auto-shed nonessential on overload; start/stabilize failure → alarm, keep UPS control power; Morrowick keeps bus within limits. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): supervisory comms, shows status, supply alarms, generator status to Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); flags work packages from Pitch Deviation Notice; gives status to permit reviewers. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): schedules/prioritizes by reviewed condition and history. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Crew Transfer Vessel (Kestrel Bay), Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel, Helideck. Vessel AIS Receiver (Blue Granite): Position Quality Flag. Personnel Tracking Console, North/South Access Scanners. Warehouse System (Mosslight): Backorder Exception Slip; Spares Hub. Metocean Buoy (Copper Finch): Wave Burst Record. Cybersecurity Gateway (Quiet Harbor): deny-by-default, RBAC, logged privileged sessions. Work Permit Portal (Redoubt): records requests, revisions, reviews, start/pause/resume/completion; returns incomplete; audit retention. Permit flow: request → Duty Planner (also Transfer Manifest Addendum) checks/submits → HSE Officer, technical reviewers, Marine Coordinator, Vessel Master review → approval scoped after reviews → Field Supervisor verifies → change → reassess/suspend → completion before closure. Actors: Control Engineer (reviews persistent alarms, coordinates with Substation Operator), Electrical Technician (verifies protection settings/interlocks), Blade Specialist, Weather Analyst, Cybersecurity Analyst, Storekeeper, Port Agent. Weather Service (Pale Lantern):

Document units:
S195: Thistle Crown schedules periodic reviews of standby electrical maintenance requirements and outstanding corrective work.
S196: After normal supply is restored, transfer back is permitted only after stable conditions are confirmed and the emergency source can be unloaded safely.
S197: The Grid Interface Relay defines the operational boundary between the offshore farm and the external transmission system.
S198: Grid Interface Relay is known operationally as Wildmere.
S199: The farm exports electrical power through the Offshore Substation, Main Transformer, and export cable to the designated grid connection point.
S200: The Export Cable Monitor provides measurements that support assessment of the export path.
S201: The Grid Interface Relay exchanges authorized operating signals with the transmission system at the agreed interface.
S202: The Grid Dispatcher sets external dispatch requirements within the applicable connection agreement.
S203: The Fleet Dispatch Console allocates requested farm output among available generating units.
S204: Dispatch commands remain subject to equipment capability, protection settings, and approved operating limits.
S205: The farm reports measured active power at the grid boundary for operational monitoring and settlement processes.
S206: Reactive power capability is managed in accordance with the connection agreement and current equipment conditions.
S207: Frequency response functions are enabled only when the relevant operating mode is authorized and available.
S208: Protection coordination prevents a fault on the external system from causing unnecessary disconnection of healthy farm equipment.
S209: Loss of communications does not remove local electrical protection or equipment interlocks.
S210: A Grid Constraint may require reduced export, revised dispatch, or temporary disconnection.
S211: SCADA Gateway provides relay status and interface measurements to the farm monitoring environment.
S212: SCADA Gateway produces the Session Revocation Receipt when an authenticated control session is terminated.
S213: Maintenance Planning Engine uses the Squall Window Bulletin when reviewing the timing of planned work.
S214: Amber Quay coordinates operational notices and control-room decisions affecting the farm interface.
S215: Kestrel Bay reports its approach and departure status in accordance with the approved marine coordination procedure.
S216: The Substation Operator confirms that switching actions affecting the export path are within the authorized work scope.
S217: The Control Engineer verifies that dispatch changes are reflected in the applicable control settings before implementation.
S218: Interface alarms are prioritized according to their effect on safety, equipment protection, and continuity of export.
S219: Planned tests are coordinated to avoid conflicting with dispatch obligations or active maintenance work.
